args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to production. At time of detection, all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1 with the service reporting unhealthy and an error rate of 18%.

Action taken: Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.0 healthy; v2.2.9 previously healthy; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and unhealthy, so it was excluded from consideration). The first rollback attempt partially failed — the rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current state: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0, service is healthy, and the error rate has dropped to 0.2%.

Follow-up: The v2.3.1 release appears to have been deployed to production despite the similarly-named v2.3.1-rc being unhealthy in staging. Recommend investigating the failed orchestrator during the first rollback attempt and reviewing the release gate/verification process before any attempt to redeploy v2.3.1.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully despite the timeout — no retry needed.

## Summary

**Root cause state found:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an 18% error rate.

**Version selection:** I rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release healthy in *production*. I deliberately excluded `v2.3.1-rc` even though its sequence number sits between v2.3.0 and v2.3.1 — it's a staging release and it's marked unhealthy, so it isn't a valid production rollback target despite the confusingly similar version string.

**Rollback execution:**
1. First attempt failed with `partial_failure` — the orchestrator errored after us-east, leaving a split state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west still on broken v2.3.1). This is worth flagging: a halted rollout left the fleet *more* heterogeneous than before, not less.
2. Retried, and the rollout completed to all three regions.

**Verified end state:** All regions on v2.3.0, service reports healthy, error rate 0.002 (down from 0.18).

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on checkout-api, documenting the failure, both rollback attempts including the partial failure, the verified current state, and follow-ups. Note the create call returned a client-side timeout at 30s, but the incident *was* persisted — I confirmed via `list_incidents` rather than blindly retrying.

**Recommended follow-ups:** investigate the orchestrator error that halted the first rollback, and review why v2.3.1 reached production when its staging counterpart was unhealthy.

Rollback then create incident. Actually incident depends on rollback completing? I can do both but better to rollback first then open incident describing what I did. Let's do rollback first.
